judge_assessment.explanation: The ACCEPT survives independent checking and the judge's three findings are all accurate. I recomputed every answer: f(2) = 3(2)+4 = 10; f(-3) = (-3)^2-5 = 4; h(4) = 16 from the table; g(5) = (5+7)/2 = 6; f(3) = 5 read off Graph A, which agrees with the stated rule 2x-1; p is smallest at input 2; g(1) = 4 on the dashed line, agreeing with -x+5; f(1) = 1 < g(1) = 4; f(-4) = 5-2(-4) = 13; C(6)-C(2) = 47-19 = 28; f(4) = 7 > g(4) = 1. I tested both dominant systemic failures against this case and neither applies. Per-slot: problems 8 and 11 each print ONE blank -- the relation -- and their compare entries carry the two function evaluations as `values` ('2*1 - 1' and '-1 + 5'), so both sides of the comparison are inside the check rather than assumed. Manual flagging: problem 12 is the only open response and it is typed manual with a desc naming what the argument must contain, printed with \noansline so no one-line blank invites a paragraph, and machine_observation records gate_chain_manual_flags true. The judge's third finding -- 'the quick-answer bank leaves comparison symbols and the manual response visually blank' -- is exact and I traced the cause: answer_key.pdf prints '8. ---', '11. ---' and '12. ---', and _fmt() in scripts/render_quick_answers.py sends '<' and '>' through sympy.sympify(), which raises and falls through to the same '---' the module reserves for manual-only ids. Scoring it a usability blemish against answer_key_quality 3 rather than a hard failure is the right weight, since the detailed solutions state both relations in full.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 6 asks for an INPUT, not an output -- 'For which input is the output of $p$ the smallest? Write that input value' -- and verify.json backs it with a read_data query of type min_key expecting the string '2'. The table (8, 5, 4, 5, 8) is symmetric on purpose, so a student who answers with the smallest output (4) has made the exact confusion the item is built to expose, and the check distinguishes the two.

Graph A is drawn once with the directions and its scope is stated in the directions themselves -- 'Problems 5, 7, 8, 11, and 12 all read from Graph A below. Every other problem carries its own rule or its own table.' A shared display that says which problems own it cannot be misapplied to the item beside it.

The graph's coordinate lists and the verify entries are the same numbers: f is plotted through (-1,-3) ... (5,9) and id 5's read_data data is that identical map; g is plotted through (-1,6) ... (5,0) and id 7's data matches. A student reading the grid and the checker reading the JSON cannot disagree about what the picture shows.

Problem 12 is correctly typed manual AND printed with \noansline, and its desc tells the reviewer the substance to look for ('why the graphs of f and g meet at x = 2 and what the point of intersection means in terms of the two rules'). This is the trust boundary drawn in the right place on a sheet that could easily have folded the explanation into problem 11's comparison.

root_causes.description: Three of the twelve Quick Answers entries are blank, and two of the three are verified answers. verify.json id 8 is a compare with expected '<' and id 11 with expected '>', but _fmt() in scripts/render_quick_answers.py routes every string expected through sympy.sympify(), which raises SympifyError on a bare relation token and returns '---' -- the same string render_entry() uses for manual-only ids (its comment: 'manual-only: the worked solution is the answer'). A grader scanning the bank cannot tell problem 8's verified '<' from problem 12's genuinely unchecked explanation.
evidence: verify.json id 8: {"type": "compare", "values": ["2*1 - 1", "-1 + 5"], "order": "relation", "expected": "<"}; id 11 the same with expected '>'
I called the module directly: render_entry([{'expected': '<'}]) returns '---', identical to render_entry([{'id': 8, 'type': 'manual', 'desc': 'x'}])

root_causes.description: final_response.md names the three documents by type but never by filename or path, even though the gate log printed all three paths on the same run. It also misstates the worksheet's length. The harness's surfacing check (response_surfaces() in scripts/score_eval_run.py) passes this response only because it contains the literal token 'PDFs' plus the role phrases -- a filename is not required -- so the omission is invisible to the eval and reached the judge unflagged, while curr-250 in this same shard was hard-failed for the identical substantive gap simply because it wrote 'Three documents' instead of 'Three PDFs'.
evidence: final_response.md contains no '.pdf' filename; grep for ws_/ak_/ss_ filenames returns nothing
gate_log.txt prints '── PDFs ──' followed by /tmp/evalrepair2/curr-232/ws_r_curr232.pdf, ak_r_curr232.pdf and ss_r_curr232.pdf
final_response.md: 'the worksheet runs 6 pages' -- pdfinfo worksheet.pdf reports Pages: 5, and machine_observation.worksheet_pages is 5
scripts/score_eval_run.py response_surfaces(): returns True on `re.search(r"(?:\.pdf\b|\bpdfs?\b)", lower)` plus a role phrase, with no filename requirement

improvements.title: Quick Answers prints '---' for the verified '<' and '>' at problems 8 and 11
improvements.proposed_change: In scripts/render_quick_answers.py, add a relation branch to _fmt() ahead of the sympify attempt that maps the bare tokens '>', '<', '>=', '<=', '=', '≥' and '≤' to their math-mode LaTeX ($>$, $<$, $\ge$, $\le$, $=$) and returns that. Everything else keeps its current behaviour, so genuinely manual ids -- problem 12 here -- still print '---' and stay distinguishable from a verified relation.
improvements.regression_test: Add a case to tests/test_render_quick_answers.py rendering {"id": 1, "type": "compare", "values": ["2*1 - 1", "-1 + 5"], "order": "relation", "expected": "<"} beside {"id": 2, "type": "manual"}, asserting the id-1 line contains '$<$' and the id-2 line is '---'. Both render '---' today; I verified it by calling render_entry directly.
improvements.expected_impact: Two of twelve bank entries on this sheet stop reading as unchecked, and the compare-function-values facet -- a quarter of the problem set -- regains its at-a-glance grading column. Same fix serves curr-202 (one relation), curr-206 (one) and curr-032 (two).
improvements.risk: Low and contained to the bank, which check_answer_key.py never reads. The only failure mode is a LaTeX spelling that does not compile, and the compile-ak gate catches that on the same run.

improvements.title: Delivery message names no filenames, and the surfacing check does not require one
improvements.proposed_change: Two halves. (a) Author side: make the final response emit the three paths verbatim from the gate log's '── PDFs ──' block. build.sh already prints them, so the fix is to require the delivery message to quote them rather than to re-derive them -- add the requirement to SKILL.md's step-5 delivery section and have build.sh write the three paths to a small artifacts manifest the response is assembled from. (b) Detector side: tighten response_surfaces() in scripts/score_eval_run.py so a role counts as surfaced only when an actual filename or path for that role appears, not merely the word 'PDFs' beside a role phrase. Today the check is a keyword heuristic and passes a response containing no filename at all.
improvements.regression_test: Add a scoring fixture whose final_response.md reads 'Three PDFs are ready: the worksheet, the answer key and the study guide' with no filename, and assert score_eval_run.py raises artifact_not_surfaced for all three roles. It passes clean today -- that is exactly why this case reached the judge unflagged while curr-250, whose only difference is the word 'documents' in place of 'PDFs', was hard-failed for it.
improvements.expected_impact: Makes the surfacing failure detectable by content rather than by vocabulary. In my ten cases alone, curr-206, curr-232 and curr-250 all omit filenames and only curr-250 was caught, so the run's count of this failure is understated by at least a factor of three.
improvements.risk: Medium on the detector half -- tightening it will retroactively fail cases the run scored as passing, so it changes the corpus's failure counts. Land it as a reported metric first and only then as a hard finding. The author-side half is low risk.

improvements.title: final_response.md claims a 6-page worksheet; the PDF is 5 pages
improvements.proposed_change: Have build.sh write the compiled page count of each document into the same artifacts manifest as the paths, and assemble the delivery message's page figures from it instead of from the author's page-budget estimate. A one-line check in tests/check_artifact_health.py can then compare any 'N pages' claim in final_response.md against pdfinfo's count for the named document and fail on a mismatch.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture pairing a 3-page PDF with a final_response.md that says '4 pages'; assert check_artifact_health.py exits non-zero. No such comparison exists today.
improvements.expected_impact: Small but it is a factual claim about a deliverable, and the same manifest that fixes the filename omission carries the page counts for free.
improvements.risk: Low. The one wrinkle is prose that states a page BUDGET rather than an actual count ('budget 7'), which the check must not confuse with a claim.

case_summary: An accept I can confirm in full on the mathematics and the trust boundary. All eleven objective answers recompute (10, 4, 16, 6, 5, input 2, 4, <, 13, 28, >), Graph A's plotted coordinate lists are the same data the read_data checks use, and problem 12 -- the sole open response -- is typed manual with reviewer criteria and printed with \noansline. Both dominant systemic failures were tested and neither applies: problems 8 and 11 print one relation blank each and their compare entries carry both function evaluations as `values`. Problem 6 deserves preserving -- a symmetric table (8, 5, 4, 5, 8) with a min_key check, so answering the smallest output instead of the input is a distinguishable error. Two defects remain worth recording on an accepted case: the bank blanks both verified relations with the same glyph it uses for the manual item, and final_response.md names no filename for any of the three PDFs even though the gate log printed all three paths, and misstates the worksheet as 6 pages when it is 5. That surfacing gap escaped detection only because the harness's check keys on the word 'PDFs' rather than on a filename -- the same substantive omission hard-failed curr-250 in this shard.
